Chapter 8. The Role of the Leader in Strategy.
When it comes to building and carrying out a great strategy, leadership really is at the heart of it all.
A leader’s job goes way beyond just pointing in the right direction. It’s about setting up the right environment—one where real strategic thinking and focused, disciplined action can happen at every level of the organization.
So, what do effective leaders actually do?
First, they make sure everyone understands the true challenge—even when that means facing up to tough, or maybe even uncomfortable, truths. Think about it. Sometimes the real issue isn’t obvious, or it’s something people just don’t want to talk about. But a good leader doesn’t shy away from that.
Next, they lay out a clear guiding policy. It’s not just about making rules—it’s about explaining the “why” behind the approach, so everyone’s on the same page and pulling in the same direction.
They also walk the talk. When leaders make decisions and act in ways that match the strategy, it sends a powerful message. People notice, and they tend to follow that lead.
But here’s something a lot of folks overlook: good leaders actually invite honest debate. They make it safe to disagree, knowing that the best solutions often come from a real back-and-forth—where people aren’t afraid to challenge each other’s thinking.
And through it all, leaders keep the team focused. There are always distractions and shiny new opportunities out there, but if you try to chase them all, you’ll lose sight of what really matters. The best leaders help everyone stay centered on the core strategy.
Picture a company that’s struggling—a true turnaround situation. The leader’s first move? They dig deep to figure out what’s really going wrong. That probably means having some hard conversations and making difficult decisions. Once they’ve got a handle on the real issues, they set a clear course. Maybe that’s doubling down on the company’s main strengths and letting go of businesses that don’t fit. By taking consistent action and communicating openly, the leader earns trust—and gets people moving together toward a better future.
At the end of the day, leadership in strategy isn’t about being the most charismatic person in the room. It’s about being clear, staying disciplined, and having the guts to make tough calls. More than anything, it’s about building a space where good strategy can actually take hold—and grow into something great.
